overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficient minutes for its April 5 meeting, ordered amended minutes, and declined to review the notice and individual-notice allegations as untimely or not covered by the law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the April 5 meeting notice topics, including the Snow Street property item, were not specific enough to inform the public.
allegations.key_passage: any complaint concerning the sufficiency of the notice for the April 5 meeting should have been filed with the Board within 30 days of that meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not give him timely individual notice of the April 5 meeting about his property.
allegations.key_passage: In addition to being untimely, this allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the April 5 minutes were insufficient, unclear on whether any vote or action occurred on the Snow Street item, and reflected none of the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the minutes are insufficient where they fail to summarize any other discussions held during the meeting, instead simply listing motions made and votes taken.

allegations.summary: To the extent the complaint alleged information should have been shared with the Chair, discussed at the meeting, and minuted, the AG declined review.
allegations.key_passage: Again, even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.

Within 30 days, amend the April 5 minutes to include a summary of all discussions, a list of all documents used, and a record of all roll call votes, and certify compliance in writing to the AG's office.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law.
